newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian shares end lower in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian shares end lower in active trade.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 16 Reuter - Colombian shares ended mostly lower in active trade that saw major selling in some financially troubled companies and profit-taking in others that posted recent gains.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index ended down 0.19 percent at 17,258.90 on above-average trading volume of about 4.6 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB closed down a razor-thin 0.04 percent, meanwhile, ending at 1,129.62 on a volume of 2.3 billion pesos. Brewing giant Bavaria, flagship of the Julio Mario Santo Domingo conglomerate, led most actives in Bogota and Medellin.

It fell victim to active profit-taking on both exchanges, a day after ING Barings said it cut the stock from buy to hold because it saw little upside following its recent rally. The stock, which has outperformed the market by 53 percent in dollar terms this year, fell 1.60 percent in Bogota to end at 7,950 pesos per share.

"It's logical for people with shares in Bavaria that they bought at 4,000 or 5,000 pesos to go out and sell," one Bogota-based broker said. Other losers included Bancoquia, Colombia's eighth largest bank, which lost 3.13 percent in Medellin to end at 3,100 pesos per share.
Dealers attributed the downward move to unexplained delays in the bank's previously announced plans to sell a 55 percent stake to Spain's Banco Santander.
Gains included Banco de Bogota, which added 3.17 percent and closed at 6,500 pesos per share on news of strong January-February earnings.
"The figures confirm that Bogota is the highest yielding bank," one broker said.

Big losers were led steel mill Acerias Paz del Rio and capital goods supplier Distral, which shed 33 percent and 32.6 percent of their share value, respectively, on local news reports describing them as at or near bankruptcy.
